rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Table 3 - the authors collect a web dataset (wheat, maize, potato; Table 1), train KNN, SVM and ANN classifiers and report accuracies of 91%, 87% and 96.81%, and build an Arduino/Raspberry Pi3 IoT system with temperature and humidity sensors that they say was tested in a potato and a wheat field.
rows.notes: The study's own results are classification accuracies of three ML algorithms on a borrowed dataset (National Institute of Technology, Raipur) for an irrigate/not-irrigate decision, plus a qualitative statement (Section 3) that the ANN-driven IoT system opened the pump only when the field needed irrigation in two test fields. No water applied, water saved or wastage is measured or compared with a conventional system; 'minimize water loss' is asserted in the title/abstract/conclusion, not demonstrated. Correct irrigation decisions are a precondition of the claimed water-conservation effect, so this is upstream evidence only. No dispersion, limitations (beyond future-work statements), or site representativeness reported.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references and biographies). The paper is a short algorithm-comparison study with a brief, unquantified field test; it is cited in the review via a different reference ([42] Jeevanantham et al.), which may indicate a citation attribution issue, but the rating is of this study's text.
